info.bio:
Third Eye Blind (frecuentemente abreviada como 3eb) es una banda de rock alternativo formada a mediados de los 90 en San Francisco. La banda está formada por Stephan Jenkins (cantante, compositor y guitarra eléctrica), Kevin Cadogan (guitarra), Brad Hargreaves (batería), and Arion Salazar (bajo). Su disco más exitoso es su homónimo "Third Eye Blind" publicado en 1997, donde se incluye su mayor éxito hasta la fecha "Semi-Charmed Life".

scenes.desc: La revolución iniciada en Chicago por Souled American y Uncle Tupelo (No Depression: baladas country con la furia del hardcore) se convierte en los noventa en un género propio: sus herederos abandonan el hardcore por los sonidos más espartanos y tradicionales. Son Volt de Jay Farrar y Wilco de Jeff Tweedy (Being There, Yankee Hotel Foxtrot); Will Oldham (Palace) arranca el movimiento; Freakwater, Ida, Handsome Family, Retsin, Blue Mountain, Whiskeytown, Grant Lee Buffalo, Citizens' Utilities, Willard Grant Conspiracy. El «chamber folk» de Lambchop, Lullaby For The Working Class, Geraldine Fibbers y Pinetop Seven; el country-rock de Volebeats, Ass Ponys, Sixteen Horsepower, Old 97's y los terroristas Grifters; el folk-rock de Swell, Counting Crows, Cracker, Cake, Hootie & The Blowfish; los Black Crowes; Belle And Sebastian, Arab Strap y los polacos Atman.

podcast.title: First-Person Lyrical Approach
podcast.body: Third Eye Blind was cited as an example of a Post-Grunge band whose lyrical style leaned heavily on the "first person approach," illustrating a key distinction from the more indirect lyrical themes of Grunge. "Now think about the lyrical writing style of collective soul or bush or third eye blind and matchbox 20. You see what I mean?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Song Origin from Speeding Friends
podcast.body: The song about crystal meth addiction was written during a period when a group of Stephen Jenkins's friends in San Francisco were constantly "speeding." "It was written at about the time when a bunch of San Francisco friends were constantly speeding."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tour Bus Bunk Description
podcast.body: Arion Salazar describes the bunks on a tour bus as small, coffin-like compartments. These bunks have curtains that can be pulled and buttoned shut, creating a "little cocoon" that serves as a private space for band members, likened to the "hellbop" concept. "We're in these little things that are like coffins, the curtains you pull them shut and button them shut and you're like securing your little cocoon."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Extensive Musician Dating History
xref.body: Winona Ryder, an actress, has been connected to or dated a significant number of musicians, totaling 22 individuals according to a count from the transcript. Her relationships included Dave Grohl, Ryan Adams, Pete Yorn, Jack White, Julian from The Strokes, Conor Oberst of Bright Eyes, possibly Jeff Tweedy from Wilco, Irish musician Damien Rice, Tre Cool of Green Day, Marky Walberg (Marky Mark), Stephen Jenkins of Third Eye Blind, Everlast (whose real name is Eric Shorty), John Kay from Jamiroquai, Adam Duritz of Counting Crows (who also dated Jennifer Aniston and Courtney Cox), Chris Isaak, Dave Pirner of Soul Asylum, Paul Westerberg of The Replacements (which was noted as potentially during her "Minneapolis punk period"), Mike Nesmith of The Monkees, Johnny Depp, and Evan Dando of The Lemonheads. The last heard connection was an engagement to Blake Sennett, who plays guitar in Rilo Kiley. "I count 22 musicians."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: Collective Soul was cited as an example of a Post-Grunge band whose lyrical writing style prominently featured a "first person approach," contrasting with the more metaphorical lyrics often found in original Grunge bands. "Now think about the lyrical writing style of collective soul or bush or third eye blind and matchbox 20. You see what I mean?"

xref.title: First-Person Lyrical Approach
xref.body: Matchbox Twenty was cited as an example of a Post-Grunge band that utilized a "first person approach" in their lyrics, a characteristic that helped define the genre's move towards more direct and accessible songwriting. "Now think about the lyrical writing style of collective soul or bush or third eye blind and matchbox 20. You see what I mean?"
